correctness.rationale: The exact mixture agrees with the published density, and backward ancestry through independent clocks also gives a total Brownian running time min(Gₙ/r,t). Sharing Gₙ and the same normal variable gives a coupling with ordered absolute displacements; the 1-Lipschitz test |x| attains its cost, proving the exact incomplete-gamma formula. At aₙ=n+z√n the square-root difference is (Gₙ−aₙ)₊/(√Gₙ+√aₙ); the standardized overshoot is uniformly integrable by its bounded second moment and the normalized denominator tends to two, giving the stated W₁ constant. For TV, after common rescaling, the first-order density difference is −n⁻¹ᐟ² E[(Hₙ−z)₊] ∂ᵥh₁, with O(n⁻¹) L¹ Taylor remainder on a compact variance interval and exponentially small density contribution from its complement. Cauchy–Schwarz also controls the complement's linear term. Half the L¹ norm of ∂ᵥh₁ is φ(1), by integrating (x²−1)φ(x) on x>1. For fixed s<1 the limiting normal variances are s and 1; density convergence at x≠0 suffices for Scheffé (the bounded-continuity argument need not apply at x=0). The density-crossing expression follows by equating the normals. For s>1 gamma concentration bounds TV by P(Gₙ>sn) and W₁ by a constant times √n times its square root. The frozen verification script was inspected without execution. Its finite TV checks are only at z=0; arbitrary z and the macroscopic TV formula are established by the proof.
